annotation.authors_or_issuer: Hosseini, E.S.; Yarijan, Y.V.; Yazdani, S.
key_provisions_or_claims: Robots lack legal or natural personhood, so humans controlling them bear compensation liability.
Islamic jurisprudence principles (la dharar, itlaf, tasbib, ghoroor) ground civil liability for robot-caused harm.
Both harmful acts and omissions by robots can trigger liability, including duty of care for objects.
Clear and comprehensive laws are needed to determine accountability and protect parties.
Autonomous AI robots may be treated as potential subjects of criminal law while other actors remain liable.
annotation.summary_en: Iranian journal article using Islamic jurisprudence to analyse civil liability for harm caused by autonomous AI-enabled robots. It concludes robots lack legal personhood, so the human controlling them must compensate, and calls for clear, comprehensive laws on accountability.
annotation.title_clean: Challenges in Realizing Civil Liability in Robotic Technology
annotation.title_en: Challenges in Realizing Civil Liability in Robotic Technology
annotation.venue: Interdisciplinary Studies in Society, Law, and Politics
